report.title: LV at DEN Week 11 Scouting Report
report.summary: Denver's pass rush and its secondary define this matchup, so LV must protect against heavy blitzes while avoiding explosive plays and third-down conversions. Denver's offense is balanced on early downs but gets predictable on third-and-long. Special teams are steady on both sides, and the kicking edge is slim, so late-game decisions matter. Finishing red zone drives will likely decide the game.

sections.heading: Opponent offense
sections.body: Denver is nearly balanced on early downs, with a 53.5% [oc1] dropback rate over 396 early-down plays [oc2]. Third-and-long is the tell, where Denver drops back on 89.7% [oc5] of snaps over 39 plays [oc6], so LV's pass rush should be ready. Pass efficiency is modest at 0.02 [oc7] EPA per pass play, but LV allows explosives on 11.3% [oc10] of plays, 32nd [oc11] in the league, so Denver's downfield shots are a real threat. Dobbins takes 47.6% [oc15] of designed rushes, while Waddle (20.1% [oc18]) and Sutton (17.8% [oc19]) lead the targets. On third down Denver converts 32.7% [oc24] over 110 [oc25] plays, while LV allows 47.4% [oc26] over 116 [oc27] plays, so third down is the key pressure point to exploit.

sections.heading: Opponent defense
sections.body: Denver brings heat, with sacks or QB hits on 20.7% [dc1] of opponent dropbacks and a 33.5% [dc3] blitz rate. LV's offense has a pressure proxy of 18.0% [dc5] over 377 [dc6] dropbacks, so pass protection will be tested. Against the run, Denver keeps 6.6 [dc8] defenders in the box and allows a 37.8% [dc10] success rate, ranking 7th [dc14] in success rate allowed. Denver allows conversions on 41.5% [dc17] of third downs over 130 [dc18] plays, and touchdowns on 51.7% [dc20] of red zone drives over 29 [dc21] drives.

sections.heading: Special teams
sections.body: Denver's field goals belong to one kicker, Wil Lutz, who has made 16 [kc1] of 19 [kc2] tries (84.2% [kc3]), so there is no kicker change to plan around. His long-range sample is tiny, at 66.7% [kc4] on 3 [kc5] attempts from long range, so treat those tries as less reliable than his short ones. Denver's punter pins opponents inside the 20 on 43.2% [kc10] of punts, so expect LV to start drives deep. Kickoffs rarely produce touchbacks, at 15.2% [kc11] on 46 [kc12], and Denver's return unit averages 26.3 [kc13] yards, so place deep kicks rather than live balls. Punt returns average only 6.3 [kc15] yards on 27 [kc16] attempts, so LV can attack the punt returner.

sections.heading: Injuries and availability
sections.body: Denver's latest injury report is the most recent available. Safety Brandon Jones is listed Out [ic1] with a hamstring injury, and he has averaged 90.8% [ic2] of snaps over 8 [ic3] games. DE Eyioma Uwazurike is also Out [ic4], at 52.1% [ic5] of snaps, and CB Kris Abrams-Draine is Out [ic7], at 35.8% [ic8]. Losing Jones and Abrams-Draine thins the secondary, so expect backups to take more snaps against LV's passing game. Safety Talanoa Hufanga is Questionable [ic10] with an ankle injury, having played 92.6% [ic11] of snaps. On LV's side, WR Dont'e Thornton Jr. is Questionable [ic19] with a back issue, and DT Thomas Booker is Questionable [ic20] with an ankle issue, playing a rotational role at 37.7% [ic21] of snaps.

sections.heading: Key matchups
sections.body: Pass rush against protection decides the early downs. Denver sends heavy blitz packages on 33.5% [mc1] of dropbacks, against LV's pressure proxy of 18.0% [mc3], so keep quick game and hot throws on the call sheet and chip with backs when the blitz comes. Third-and-long is LV's best spot: Denver drops back on 89.7% [mc5] of those snaps, and LV allows conversions on 47.4% [mc7] of third downs. Explosives are LV's leak, with 11.3% [mc8] allowed, 32nd [mc9] in the league. Shade safeties toward Waddle (20.1% [mc11]) and Sutton (17.8% [mc12]), since Denver's play action rate is 22.2% [mc13]. In the red zone, Denver scores on 65.4% [mc14] of drives against LV's 70.0% [mc16] allowed, so force Denver to settle for field goals rather than touchdowns.
